title: The Three-Legged Stool
story:
Morning arrived in Aldea San Gabriel with a cool draft carrying the scent of pine smoke and damp earth. James awoke in his cedar bed beneath the mossy tiles of the old shed, watching golden beams of sunlight slice through the gaps in the timber walls. Beside him, his carefully arranged shelf held his gathered treasures—the brass cog, the green sea-glass, the clay whistle—each resting in its own small notch of cedar dust.

He had learned the morning rhythm of the village now. He had learned the rasp of Don Tadeo's hand plane against raw cedar. He had learned the chattering call of the mountain jays in the jacaranda tree. He had learned the low, rhythmic clatter of clay coffee mugs from the neighboring kitchen. Stepping out into the cool air, James trotted over to the open-air workshop, where this man was already sorting through a pile of smooth wood offcuts.

Noticing James, the carpenter set aside three rounded wooden pegs and a small slab of planed cedar wood. With patient gestures, he showed James how to rub coarse sand-leaf over the rough edges until the wood felt soft and slick as river stone. James worked diligently, his nimble hands moving back and forth, smoothing away every tiny splinter with steady concentration.

By mid-morning, with a few light taps of a wooden mallet, the three pegs were snug in the base of the cedar slab. James carried the tiny three-legged stool back into his shed and set it carefully beside his shelf. Sitting atop his very first piece of crafted furniture inside his very own home, he pulled out his green sea-glass, looking through it as the sunlight turned the quiet room into a glowing emerald sanctuary.
